messages:
maria: Heads-up — canary (autotune/v2.3.1) shows a regression on long sequences. p99 for >1024 tokens increased ~18% compared to baseline. Leaving traces below, anyone else seeing this?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout completed 2026-03-18T10:10:12Z (autotune/v2.3.1). release: https://ci.redwood/roll/4582 :rocket:

akshay: Looking now. Can you paste the runtime telemetry dump — specifically kernel_router.choice, kernel_router.reason, and any kv cache metrics around the spike?

maria: Paste of compact telemetry (sanitized):
```
kernel_router.choice: "megapack_gemm_v2"
kernel_router.reason: "predicted_latency_low"
kernel_router.pick_score: 0.74
seq_len_bucket: ">1024"
batch_policy.target_batch: 48
kv_cache.hit_rate: 0.62 -> 0.58 (during spike)
measured_latency_ms.p99: 248 (baseline 210)
gpu_util: 76% -> 92%
mem_pressure: high
```

jon: Interesting — kv_cache.hit_rate drops when choice flips to megapack_gemm_v2. That suggests either the kernel's memory layout is incompatible with our KV layout or the batch growth is causing eviction thrash.

lee: Also note the batching optimizer bumped target_batch for long sequences from 32 -> 48 in this rollout (policy tweak). Increasing batch size increases working set; on some archs that forces fallback or causes more memory copies.

akshay: Repro command I used locally (with debug flags):
```bash
REDWOOD_KR_DEBUG=1 REDWOOD_BATCH_DEBUG=trace REDWOOD_KV_TRACE=1 \
./perf_harness --model gpt-small --seq 1200 --qps 5 --duration 5m --capture-telemetry=kernel_router,kvcache,profiler
```
This reproduces p99 regression consistently for me in staging.

perf-bot: perf-bot: profiler upload: https://profiler.redwood/trace/987654 (samples show spike in memcpy and L2 cache misses aligned with kernel switch)

maria: Run numbers from staging run: p50 45ms (unchanged), p95 118ms -> 132ms, p99 210ms -> 248ms, observed ~15% more GPU memcpy time and ~25% higher L2 misses during megav2 window.

jon: Hypothesis: pick_score model underestimated the memory-copy / cache-warmup cost for megapack_gemm_v2 at high seq_len and larger batches. Autotune objective seemed to prefer throughput, not the combined KV locality cost.

lee: Temporary mitigation: add a conservative safe-mode gate for autotune that prevents cross-architecture aggressive kernels for seq_len > 512 or when kv_hit_rate < 0.7. We can flip this env flag for canary revert.

akshay: Add these telemetry changes before re-enabling autotune: emit predicted_cost and measured_cost for each decision, plus kernel_choice->kv_hit_rate histogram. Without those we can't close the loop.

maria: Agreed. Action items:
- lee: open PR to add telemetry fields (predicted_cost, measured_cost) and safe-mode env (REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE_SAFE_MODE=1) — then revert canary.
- akshay: run 30m perf job with the debug flags and attach flamegraphs.
- maria: prepare replay harness and run the regression replay against the canary image in staging.
- jon: triage the kernel source for memcpy/memory-layout changes in v2.3.1 (I saw a macro change in PR #4567 that might be related).

jon: :+1: I'll start digging into PR #4567 now and post findings.

lee: I'll sketch the telemetry schema and open the PR in the next hour. tagging @akshay @maria for review. :eyes:

maria: Thanks all — if anyone finds a quick hotfix (e.g., short-term env flip) post here and I'll coordinate the canary rollback.
